facts.statement: Nanningosaurus is a hadrosauromorph dinosaur found in the Nalong Basin of Guangxi, China.
facts.quote: Nanningosaurus is a genus of hadrosauromorph dinosaur from the upper Late Cretaceous of the Nalong Basin, Guangxi, China.

facts.statement: The only known species, Nanningosaurus dashiensis, was named and described by Mo Jinyou and colleagues in 2007.
facts.quote: The type and only species is Nanningosaurus dashiensis, named and described by Mo Jinyou, Zhao Zhongru, Wamg Wei, and Xu Xing in 2007.

facts.statement: The genus name Nanningosaurus refers to the city of Nanning near the excavation site.
facts.quote: The generic name refers to the city of Nanning, located close to the excavation site.

facts.statement: The holotype NHMG8142 is an incomplete skeleton found in 1991 that includes the skull, arm, leg, and pelvis.
facts.quote: Nanningosaurus is based on the holotype, NHMG8142, an incomplete skeleton including skull, arm, leg, and pelvis remains found in 1991, together with the holotype of Qingxiusaurus.

facts.statement: The fossil discoveries were reported in scientific literature in 1998.
facts.quote: The discoveries were in 1998 reported in the scientific literature.

facts.statement: The paratype specimen NHJM8143 consists of a right maxilla.
facts.quote: The paratype is NHJM8143, a right maxilla.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated the body length at 7.5 meters and weight at 2.5 tonnes in 2010.
facts.quote: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the body length of Nanningosaurus at 7.5 m and its weight at 2.5 t.

facts.statement: Diagnostic features include a high and sharp ascending maxilla branch, twenty-seven tooth positions in the maxilla, a wide lower quadrate, a gracile upper arm, and a curved ischium.
facts.quote: a unique combination of diagnostic characteristics includes a high and sharp ascending branch of the maxilla, a short rear branch of the maxilla, relatively few tooth positions (twenty-seven in the maxilla), a transversely wide lower quadrate with a weak paraquadratic notch, a gracile upper arm, and an ischium that at the lower end of its rear edge curves towards its expanded tip.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Nanningosaurus was a basal lambeosaurine, though they noted the support for this classification was tentative.
facts.quote: Mo et al. (2007), who described the specimen, performed a phylogenetic analysis that suggests Nanningosaurus was a basal lambeosaurine, although they stressed the support for this was tentative.

facts.statement: Nanningosaurus was the first hadrosauroid dinosaur named from southern China.
facts.quote: This animal was the first hadrosauroid named from southern China.

facts.statement: Nanningosaurus is classified within the family Hadrosauridae.
Nanningosaurus belongs to the subfamily Lambeosaurinae.
Nanningosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, between 72 and 66 million years ago in the Maastrichtian stage.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, entre 72 Y 66 millones de años, en el Maastrichtiense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: The time range for Nanningosaurus is estimated from the Cenomanian to the Maastrichtian, between 100.5 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Maastrichtian (100.5 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.quote: The specific name is derived from the Pinyin da-shi ('great stone'), the name of the village where the discovery was made.
